name: device-approval
title: Device Approval
description: DeviceApproval: approve or deny a device that asked to pair. It shows the device's name, kind and detail, the pairing code through PairingCode with its comparison, a security warning, what the device gets and what it asked for but won't get (with why), items the person ticks to include (a marked one, like a replacement, needs its own confirmation), a countdown to the request's expiry, and Approve and Deny with pending and error states. Approve waits for a person when an agent presses it, stays off while the codes don't match, nothing is selected or a replacement isn't confirmed, and after expiry; agents never read or type the code.
docs:
`<DeviceApproval device={{ name: "Studio laptop", kind: "Desktop", detail: "Asked 2 minutes ago" }} code="BCDF-GHJK" compare="enter" compareText={{ label: "Code on your device", matches: "Codes match", mismatch: "Codes don't match" }} granted={[{ id: "read", label: "Read projects" }]} withheld={[{ id: "admin", label: "Manage members", reason: "Your role can't grant this" }]} warning="Only approve a device you're holding." expiresAt={request.expiresAt} onExpire={refresh} onApprove={() => api.approve(id)} onDeny={() => api.deny(id)} text={{ granted: "It will be able to", withheld: "It asked for, but won't get", approve: "Approve", deny: "Deny", approveAgentConfirm: "Gives Studio laptop access to your workspace", error: "The decision couldn't be sent.", expiresIn: (_ms, time) => `Expires in ${time}`, expired: "This request has expired." }} />`.

**Permissions.** `granted` and `withheld` are `{ id, label, description?, reason? }`: two lists named by their headings (`text.granted`, `text.withheld`), side by side on a wide container, a tick on success for what it gets and a ban sign on warning for what it won't. An empty list leaves its section out.

**Decision.** `onApprove` and `onDeny` may return a Promise: the block is busy and the other button off until it settles; a rejection with a string or a React node shows it as it is in a live destructive Alert ("This device is already paired with another account."), anything else shows `text.error`, which can also be a function of the error, and `text.approved`/`text.denied` show once it's accepted. Or pass `actions`, a node or `(state) => node` with `{ expired, codesMatch, approveBlocked }`, for your own; mark your approve control with `data-agent-confirm`.

**Agents.** Approve carries `data-agent-confirm` (`text.approveAgentConfirm`), so an agent's `approve` waits for a person; the block's own `deny` doesn't. With `code` and `compare`, Approve stays off until the codes match, and an agent's approve fails the step with why.

**Blocked by the app.** `approveBlocked` turns Approve off for a reason of your own, like an account that can't grant any requested permission, and wins over the comparison. `approveBlockedReason` is a string in the page's language: it shows beside the actions, describes Approve (`aria-describedby`) and is the message an agent's `approve` fails with, so the person and the agent read the same words; it's a string so an agent always gets text. Without it nothing shows and an agent hears an English reason. Deny stays available, and `actions` gets `approveBlocked` in its state. `agentHidden` is on by default here: agents never read the code, copy it, answer the comparison or type into its field; `agentHidden={false}` turns that off.

**Expiry.** `expiresAt` (a Date or epoch ms) shows `text.expiresIn(remainingMs, "m:ss")` each second in a `role="timer"` (not live), and announces it politely once a minute and at 30, 20 and 10 seconds. One timeout per second runs while the page is visible and none while it's hidden. When it passes, Approve and Deny turn off (an agent's step fails with "the request has expired"), `text.expired` shows and is announced, and `onExpire` runs once. Every visible word comes from `text`; `labels.code` names the code, in English by default (`text.code` wins over it), and `codeLabels` is the inner PairingCode's `labels` (its copy button, `copied`, `copiedAnnouncement` and `spell`), merged over PairingCode's English defaults. The comparison field takes its label from `compareText.label`, so it needs no labels of its own.

**Items.** `items` lists things the person ticks to include, like keys to upload: `{ id, label, description?, detail?, disabled?: { reason }, marker?: { label, confirm } }`, under `text.items`, beside `granted` and `withheld`. Each is a CheckboxRow; `detail` sits at the end of the row (a `SecretFingerprint`, say), and a disabled item shows its reason. `selected`/`defaultSelected` hold the ids and `onSelectedChange(ids, details)` reports them. `onApprove` then receives `{ selected, confirmed }`; a callback that takes no arguments keeps working.

A `marker` is for an item that replaces something that already exists: `marker.label` shows as a warning Badge ("Replace"), and once the item is selected a second checkbox labelled `marker.confirm` ("Replace the existing key") appears in a group of confirmations under the list. Approve stays off while nothing is selected (`text.nothingSelected`) and until every selected marked item has its confirmation ticked (`text.unconfirmed`, a string or a function of the labels), or is deselected; the reason shows beside the actions, describes Approve and is what an agent's `approve` fails with (an English one when the text is missing, with nothing shown). Deselecting a marked item clears its confirmation, so selecting it again needs a new tick; `confirmed` lists only the selected marked items with their confirmation ticked.

**Agents and items.** The items group (named by `text.items`, or `labels.items`) has `select(idOrLabel, checked = true)`, by label in any case or id, with no person needed, and reads `selected`. The confirmations group (`labels.markers`) carries `data-agent-confirm` (`labels.confirmMarkers`), so its `confirmMarker(idOrLabel, checked = true)` waits for a person like Approve. An unknown item, a disabled one (with its reason), a confirmation for an item that isn't selected or isn't marked, and any change after the decision fail the step with why. The checkboxes themselves carry `data-agent-hidden`.
